Literal must match 大司農丞 as assistant director of the Grand Minister of Agriculture, not Ministry of Revenue.
Before long he was made expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and shortly thereafter was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.
Before long he was appointed academician recipient of edicts, and shortly thereafter was appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.
承旨學士 is academician recipient of edicts; expositor would be 侍讀/侍講.

The following year he received the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with appointments as expositor of the Hanlin Academy, controller of imperial edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.

The following year he received the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with appointments as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, controller of imperial edicts, and concurrent compiler of the national history.
翰林學士承旨 is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, not expositor.
The next year he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Hanlin Academician Expositor, Controller of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
The next year he was granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, Controller of Imperial Edicts, and concurrent Compiler of the National History.
Literal Expositor mistranslates 承旨; Recipient of Edicts is required.

後主禪 uses 禪 as Liu Shan's personal name, not 'abdicates'; 昭烈 is Zhaolie, not the Latter Lord.

Second: in the third year of Zhangwu the Huizhou edition writes in large characters 'third year; the Later Lord abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' whereas the Jian edition lacks 'third year,' which would make the Latter Lord have no end.

Second: in the third year of Zhangwu the Huizhou edition writes in large characters 'third year; Later Lord Shan, first year of Jianxing,' whereas the Jian edition lacks 'third year,' which would make Zhaolie have no end.
Literal must read Later Lord Shan and Zhaolie; 禪 is the given name and 昭烈 is not the Latter Lord.

Under the third year one should note 'Emperor Shan, first year of Jianxing,' and the following year head the entry 'Emperor Shan, second year of Jianxing,' so that the sequence is internally consistent.
帝禪 means Emperor Shan (劉禪), with 禪 as the personal name, not the verb 'abdicates'.

One should under the third year add the note 'the Emperor abdicates, first year of Jianxing,' and the next year write in large characters 'the Emperor abdicates, second year of Jianxing,' so that before and after there is no contradiction.

One should under the third year add the note 'Emperor Shan, first year of Jianxing,' and the next year write in large characters 'Emperor Shan, second year of Jianxing,' so that before and after there is no contradiction.
Literal 帝禪 is Emperor Shan, not 'the Emperor abdicates'.

If again a Ban Mengjian should appear, tabulating men ancient and modern, he would surely place Master Ouyang in the first rank of the nine grades; then though removed from the sages and worthies, there would be degrees yet not great distance; though his writing lacked the discernment of Xie and Yin, it would not harm his standing among posterity.
班孟堅 is Ban Gu's courtesy name Mengjian; Menjian is a corrupt romanization.
The king of Korea, the Prince of Shenyang, and his son were then allied to the imperial house by marriage and spent lavishly to win over courtiers.
The Goryeo Prince of Shenyang and his son were then allied to the imperial house by marriage and spent lavishly to win over courtiers.
高麗瀋陽王父子 is one father-son pair (the Goryeo Prince of Shenyang and his son), not a separate king of Korea plus the prince.

In the second year of Zhida (1309) Renzong visited Mount Wutai; Guo Guan was presented to him, and Renzong asked: "How did the integrity commissioner Mielijitai win a reputation for good government?"
至大 is the Zhida reign; Zhide is a different reign name.
In the second year of Zhide Renzong came to Mount Wutai; Guan presented himself for audience, and Renzong thereupon asked: "How did the integrity commissioner Mielijitai achieve good government?"
In the second year of Zhida Renzong came to Mount Wutai; Guan presented himself for audience, and Renzong thereupon asked: "How did the integrity commissioner Mielijitai achieve good government?"
Literal must render 至大 as Zhida, not Zhide.

In the first year of Taiding (1324) he was offered Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts but declined to serve.

In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor but did not take up the post.
In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts but did not take up the post.

Orphaned in youth, he was taken by his maternal uncle Du to Dongping, where he studied under Kang Ye.
舅杜氏 names a maternal uncle of the Du surname; 'uncle's family' omits both kinship line and surname.

Yuzong was then heir apparent; whenever Zhiqi attended audience he was given a seat and treated with marked favor.
裕宗 is Zhenjin’s temple name Yuzong, not Emperor Chengzong (成宗/Temür).

Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a native of Mingshui.

Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a man of Moshui.
Liu Geng, styled Xizai, was a man of Mingshui.

In the second year of Zhida (1309) he was made Minister of Rites while retaining his Hanlin academician post.

In the second year of Zhida he was transferred to Minister of Rites while still holding the Hanlin academician post concurrently.
Literal must render 至大 as Zhida, not Zhide.
